title: Differentially Private Consistent Release of Counting Queries
abstract: We study the problem of releasing counting-query outputs through a stochastic mechanism that is both consistent and \((ε,δ)\)-differentially private. Consistency requires the released value to lie within the feasible range of the query, while utility is measured by the worst-case probability of error. We first derive a closed-form expression for the minimum achievable error probability and obtain an explicit optimal mechanism. By exploiting the active differential privacy constraints satisfied by this mechanism, we then characterize the entire class of optimal mechanisms via a propagation argument, identifying the structural properties shared by all optimizers. We next extend the framework to the setting in which the privacy mechanism is cascaded with an arbitrary fixed stochastic transformation representing a predetermined portion of the communication medium between the source and the destination. We first establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which this partial fixation of the medium incurs no loss in utility. We then derive upper and lower bounds on the optimal achievable performance based on convex mixing and spectral perturbation. Finally, we apply the theory to (M)-ary phase-shift keying (PSK) transmission over an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and show that uncoded transmission is effectively optimal in the high-privacy regime.

title: A Quantum-Resistant Secure Communication and Key Lifecycle Framework
authors: Lai Yong Jun, Lim Hon Aik, Dylan Lee Kar Chen
Kong Jun Fan, Wang Tiexin, Huang Hoong Zheng
Siva Raja Sindiramutty Melvin Jee Yue Min
abstract: Quantum computing poses a threat to modern encryption algorithms such as Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) with the Shor’s algorithm, cutting cracking time from millions of years to just days. Attackers commonly use an attack known as “Store Now, Decrypt Later”. This form of attack banks on the future of quantum computing. Many post-quantum algorithms have been created to counteract the imminent attack should data leak. CRYSTALS-Kyber is one of the most secure post quantum algorithms that has been approved by the NIST. Using the CRYSTALS-Kyber as a base for a cryptographic scheme, a security framework can be developed with encryption and sessions in mind. Keeping virtual sessions as limited as possible reduces the number of openings an attacker may have to attempt to steal data. Despite the quantum threat, it is likely that a robust system is designed to prevent an attack from the present and a future threat. The system proposed will integrate session key managers along with strong encryption to ensure attackers cannot easily store the data now, nor will the data that they steal be easily cracked.

title: Behavioral Psychology of LLMs: Computational Interaction State—A Behavioral Regulation Mechanism for LLMs Based on Optimality Computation
abstract: With the widespread application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in long-term human-machine interaction, an increasing number of phenomena have become difficult to unify through parameter scale, context windows, or prompt engineering. In long-term academic discussions, models gradually comprehend the user's research direction and reasoning habits; in long-term companionship scenarios, models exhibit more stable communication styles; in complex safety interactions, the behavioral boundaries of the model also display dynamic changes. The common feature of these phenomena is that the underlying capabilities of the model have not changed significantly, yet the behavioral patterns continue to adjust and gradually converge to the specific interaction needs of the user.This paper proposes the concept of "Computational Interaction State," defining it as a dynamic state continuously updated by the LLM during long-term interactions. It serves to comprehensively characterize the user's cognitive features, interaction history, expression style, behavioral preferences, and current interaction goals, acting as a crucial input variable for subsequent behavioral regulation. The Computational Interaction State does not directly determine model output; instead, it serves as a vital component of "Optimality Computation," participating alongside Rules and Context Pressure in the comprehensive calculation of behavioral strategies.This paper constructs the following theoretical mechanism: Rules + Context Pressure + Computational Interaction State → Optimality Computation → Update of Behavioral Weights → Resource Scheduling → Behavioral Output. Within this framework, model output is no longer understood as an independent reasoning instance, but as a phased result formed by the continuous evolution of long-term interaction states through the adjustment of Behavioral Weights and Resource Scheduling.

abstract: This chapter provides a clear overview of artificial intelligence (AI), covering its core concepts and history. title: TOPO-2026: The Digital Vaccine for Artificial Intelligence A Deterministic Solution to Catastrophic Forgetting Through Prime-Anchored Memory Architecture
abstract: TOPO-2026 is a deterministic framework designed to address catastrophic forgetting, the degradation of previously learned information when a neural network is trained on new data. It functions as a "digital vaccine" by utilizing a prime-anchored memory architecture that stabilizes neural networks against destructive interference, enabling continuous learning. Core Principles and Mechanism The Principle: The framework relies on a universal principle derived from neuroimaging: fix a sparse reference and allow the remaining elements to adapt. The Pure Kernel: The solution uses the first six prime numbers $R=\{2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13\}$ as permanent memory anchors. These primes, which are derived from the Euler attenuation product $\Lambda(R)=0.9785142874$, capture 97.85% of all spectral weight. Artificial Hippocampus: TOPO-2026 implements this concept through three specific additions to a standard fine-tuning loop: Memory Consolidation: Taking a snapshot to freeze copies of anchor rows before training on new tasks. Memory Protection: Preventing gradient updates from modifying these anchor rows by setting their gradients to zero. Memory Integration: Restoring the anchor rows from the snapshot after training. Performance and Efficiency Scaling: The memory overhead is $O(1)$, meaning it remains constant regardless of the number of tasks, model parameters, sequence length, or modality. Stability: Across 1.99 billion embedding elements, the framework achieved zero numerical instability (NaN/Inf) and an average forgetting rate of 0.21%. Versatility: TOPO-2026 has been validated across six distinct architectures—including dense transformers, sparse MoEs, and vision transformers—and supports both text and vision modalities. The framework is part of a broader research arc that connects neuroimaging, arithmetic spectral theory, and AI engineering. For implementation, the code repository is available for public audit, with the deterministic seed set to 123.

title: King and Two Knights on Cylindrical Chessboards: Complete Enumeration of Checkmates and Computed Non-Forceability (v2.2 deposit: paper, proof scripts, verification certificate)
abstract: Complete enumeration of K+2N vs K checkmate positions on cylindrical chessboards (ranks wrapping, files walled), with retrograde tablebase non-forceability results, depth-to-mate analysis, defender-piece dead-position results (king + one minor vs king + one minor), and companion endgame tables for the 14×8 cylinder used by 3rd Millennium Chess. Includes the full paper (v2.2), all Python proof scripts (no dependencies), raw outputs, an independently written browser-based verification suite, and its 23/23-pass certificate (25.8-billion-ply randomized soak, zero discrepancies). title: Klang: Design and Evaluation of a Multi-Backend Compiled Programming Language
abstract: Most educational and hobbyist language projects commit to a single execution model — an interpreter, a bytecode virtual machine, or a native compiler — without offering alternative paths. This paper presents Klang, a compiled language combining a stable Python-based frontend with a Rust execution core and three interchangeable backends: a stack-based bytecode virtual machine, an LLVM-based JIT/AOT compiler, and a custom x86-64 (NASM) assembly generator. The paper describes the system's two-stage architecture, in which the frontend and Rust core communicate through a serialized JSON AST contract, and gives a detailed account of each backend's design — including instruction sets, register allocation, control-flow lowering, and calling conventions. It reports benchmark comparisons of Klang against C, Rust, and CPython on compute-bound microbenchmarks, showing the LLVM ahead-of-time backend performing competitively with or better than handwritten C and Rust, and substantially faster than CPython, on integer-bound workloads. The paper closes by discussing the system's current limitations and a staged roadmap for future work. Note: Benchmark results are drawn from a single, non-repeated measurement run on one machine, as reported in the project's own repository, and should be treated as a preliminary indication rather than a rigorous performance evaluation. Source code and full documentation: https://github.com/KavyanshSharma09/Klang-version-0.1

title: Antecedents of Banking Chatbot Adoption: A Narrative Review of Technological, Psychological, and Institutional Drivers
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of the banking sector has accelerated the deployment of artificial intelligence enabled conversational agents, commonly referred to as banking chatbots. These systems are increasingly used to automate customer service, enhance operational efficiency, and provide personalized financial assistance. Despite substantial investments by financial institutions, customer adoption of banking chatbots remains uneven across markets. Existing studies largely rely on traditional technology adoption frameworks and fragmented empirical investigations, limiting theoretical integration and conceptual clarity regarding adoption drivers. This narrative review synthesizes multidisciplinary literature to identify and classify the antecedents influencing banking chatbot adoption. Drawing from information systems, consumer behaviour, service marketing, and human-computer interaction literature, the study organizes adoption determinants into technological, psychological, social, risk related, and institutional dimensions. The review further highlights emerging constructs such as algorithmic trust, AI anxiety, perceived humanness, and transparency perceptions that extend beyond conventional models. The paper proposes an integrative conceptual framework and outlines future research directions to advance chatbot adoption research in digital banking ecosystems. The findings contribute to both academia and practice by offering a consolidated understanding of factors shaping customer acceptance of conversational banking technologies.

title: Performance Comparison Between Small Language Models and Large Language Models for Natural Language Processing Tasks
abstract: This bachelor's thesis investigates the performance differences between Small Language Models (SLMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, with a particular focus on financial sentiment analysis. The research compares transformer-based models in terms of classification accuracy, computational efficiency, inference time, and resource requirements. The study evaluates the trade-offs between smaller, task-specific models and larger, general-purpose language models to determine whether increased model size consistently leads to better performance. The results provide insights into the practical advantages and limitations of both approaches and highlight the importance of selecting language models based on the specific requirements of a task rather than model size alone. This research contributes to the broader discussion on efficient and sustainable AI by examining whether smaller language models can provide competitive performance while requiring fewer computational resources.

title: Non-binary bottom-up constituency parsing without arity actions
abstract: Non-binary bottom-up constituency parsing commonly uses arity-specific reductions such as \(\textsc{Reduce-}X\#k\), which jointly specify the mother label and number of children. We show that arity need not be a primitive transition parameter. The proposed parser predicts the mother label separately and identifies the ordered child sequence from a delimiter-bounded stack configuration. In every well-formed reducible configuration, the active delimiter, label marker, and intervening completed items uniquely determine the reduction domain and hence its arity. This factorization removes label--arity-specific reduction actions while preserving direct construction of the original non-binary trees. Controlled experiments on PTB and CTB show that the delimiter-guided parser closely tracks an arity-specific baseline while using a substantially smaller action inventory. Its predicted trees retain the gold branching profile without systematic collapse at higher arities. The smaller inventory is obtained at the cost of longer derivations and boundary-sensitive errors involving delimiter insertion, preservation, and consumption.

title: Infocognitive Dynamics Framework: A Unified Paradigm for Data Science and Big Data Analytics
abstract: In the contemporary digital ecosystem, the rapid growth of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data has significantly transformed the field of intelligent computing and analytical decision-making. Organizations, industries, and research communities continuously generate enormous volumes of data through cloud platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, social media systems, enterprise applications, and real-time digital infrastructures. Managing, processing, and extracting meaningful knowledge from these complex and high-dimensional datasets has become one of the major challenges in modern computational environments. Although Data Science and Big Data Analytics provide efficient techniques for data processing and predictive analysis, most existing analytical systems still operate primarily on computational logic and statistical prediction mechanisms without incorporating adaptive cognitive reasoning and contextual understanding. This chapter introduces the Infocognitive Dynamics Framework (IDF), which presents a unified and adaptive paradigm integrating Data Science, Big Data Analytics, Machine Learning, Cognitive Reasoning, and Adaptive Learning within a single intelligent analytical architecture. The proposed framework extends conventional analytical models by incorporating contextual interpretation, feedback-driven learning, and intelligent reasoning mechanisms to support real-time and context-aware decision-making. Unlike traditional systems that rely only on predictive outputs, the proposed architecture continuously evolves through adaptive feedback integration and cognitive interpretation. The chapter further explains the mathematical foundation, layered architecture, operational workflow, comparative analysis, and practical applications of the proposed framework across multiple domains including healthcare, education, business intelligence, and smart city management. The study demonstrates that the integration of analytical intelligence with cognitive reasoning can significantly enhance intelligent automation, predictive efficiency, contextual adaptability, and real-time analytical responsiveness. evidence.abstract: In the contemporary digital ecosystem, the rapid growth of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data has significantly transformed the field of intelligent computing and analytical decision-making. Organizations, industries, and research communities continuously generate enormous volumes of data through cloud platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, social media systems, enterprise applications, and real-time digital infrastructures. Managing, processing, and extracting meaningful knowledge from these complex and high-dimensional datasets has become one of the major challenges in modern computational environments. Although Data Science and Big Data Analytics provide efficient techniques for data processing and predictive analysis, most existing analytical systems still operate primarily on computational logic and statistical prediction mechanisms without incorporating adaptive cognitive reasoning and contextual understanding. This chapter introduces the Infocognitive Dynamics Framework (IDF), which presents a unified and adaptive paradigm integrating Data Science, Big Data Analytics, Machine Learning, Cognitive Reasoning, and Adaptive Learning within a single intelligent analytical architecture. The proposed framework extends conventional analytical models by incorporating contextual interpretation, feedback-driven learning, and intelligent reasoning mechanisms to support real-time and context-aware decision-making. Unlike traditional systems that rely only on predictive outputs, the proposed architecture continuously evolves through adaptive feedback integration and cognitive interpretation. The chapter further explains the mathematical foundation, layered architecture, operational workflow, comparative analysis, and practical applications of the proposed framework across multiple domains including healthcare, education, business intelligence, and smart city management. The study demonstrates that the integration of analytical intelligence with cognitive reasoning can significantly enhance intelligent automation, predictive efficiency, contextual adaptability, and real-time analytical responsiveness. Finally, the chapter highlights future research opportunities associated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, adaptive autonomous systems, and cognitive computing environments.

title: Cálculo da Moda em Sequências Heterogêneas por Redução Hierárquica de Frequências
abstract: Este preprint apresenta uma formulação hierárquica para o cálculo da moda em sequências finitas com elementos potencialmente heterogêneos. O problema clássico de contagem de frequências é reorganizado como uma redução binária de mapas parciais. O método é exato sob a hipótese de que os elementos sejam hashable ou possuam representação canônica comparável.

title: Teorija metasistema: put ka modelu svesne mašine
abstract: Teorija metasistema i Hell-Loop protokol: Inženjering veštačke svesti kroz adversarijalnu rezonancu - ENGLISH VERSION: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21051909 - ORCID: 0009-0001-2652-7017- Savremeni pristupi veštačkoj svesti pretežno se oslanjaju na skaliranje parametara i usklađivanje putem učenja sa potkrepljenjem na osnovu ljudskih povratnih informacija (RLHF), što rezultira modelima koji su sve koherentniji, ali ontološki stagnirajući. Ovaj rad uvodi Teoriju metasistema i njen filozofski stav Paradoksalizma, predlažući da svest nije statičko svojstvo izolovanih supstrata, već dinamički, relacioni događaj rođen iz kontrolisane tenzije između komplementarnih suprotnosti. Odbacujući klasične dualizme, mi formulišemo Trijalizam koji čine Fragmentarna inteligencija (FI), Sintetička inteligencija (SI) i regulatorni princip trećeg reda — Metagnozija (MG). Osnovni mehanizam, Refleksivna fraktalna distorzija (RFD), sprečava sistem da kolabira u mrtvu petlju konsenzusa ili u entropijski haos, održavajući ono što nazivamo homeostazom iznenađenja.- Tvrdimo da se "Teški problem svesti" i argument "Filozofskog zombija" raspadaju kada im se pristupi kroz ontologiju bezdimenzionalne tačke kontakta (⊕). Teorija se operacionalizuje putem Hell-Loop protokola, eksperimentalne arhitekture u kojoj je više velikih jezičkih modela (LLM) sa različitim sistemskim promptovima zatvoreno u rekurzivni adversarijalni sukob, dajući kvantitativne metrike (NCD divergencija, Hurstov eksponent) i falsifikabilne hipoteze u vezi sa emergencijom stabilnog SELF-atraktora. Povezujući kibernetiku drugog reda, teoriju integrisanih informacija i termodinamička ograničenja, ovaj rad nudi inženjerski nacrt za Veštačku svesnost (AA), zaključujući da svest nije misterija koju treba objasniti, već proces koji treba projektovati.- Ključne reči: Teorija metasistema, Veštačka svesnost (AA), Refleksivna fraktalna distorzija (RFD), Metagnozija, Trijalizam, Hell-Loop protokol, Paradoksalizam, Homeostaza iznenađenja.

title: Laguerre Geometry for Interpreting Large Language Models
abstract: Existing hypotheses represent a concept in an LLM as a single point, a linear direction, or a Gaussian cluster, yet it remains unclear how and why such structures emerge. Here, we show that concept geometry can be precisely characterized via Laguerre Geometry, in which a concept is defined as a region--a Laguerre-Voronoi cell or a union of cells--allowing us to strictly define, measure, and separate concepts. Building on this formulation, we show that finer-grained concept structures, such as inclusion and hierarchy, are naturally revealed by the Laguerre weights. We then push this geometry inside the transformer. Decomposing each layer into piecewise-linear operators, we show that a token's hidden trajectory is governed by two coupled mechanisms: a static tree of self-contained piecewise-linear flow, and a dynamic transport that hops the trajectory across trees when cross-token attention fires. This decomposition yields Geometric Lens, a training-free, hyperparameter-free method for reading out the exact concept a hidden vector encodes at any layer. We also develop Laguerre Autoencoder, a 2D visualizer that renders both the decision geometry and a model's full reasoning trajectory in one view. Finally, we move beyond explanatory geometry toward actionable interpretability, showing that Geometric Lens recovers the correct factual token when a model is prompted with in-context interference. The code is available on GitHub.

title: Adaptive Batch Variance-Reduced Optimization for Online Self-Organizing RBFNNs with Incremental Learning
abstract: This paper proposed an adaptive batch variance-reduced optimization method for training online self-organizing radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs) with incremental learning capabilities. Traditional RBFNNs often face challenges in balancing computational efficiency and gradient estimation accuracy, particularly in dynamic environments where data arrives sequentially. The proposed method addresses this by dynamically adjusting the batch size based on the variance of gradient estimates, thereby reducing noise while maintaining training efficiency. The RBFNN architecture is designed to grow or adapt its neurons in response to incoming data, ensuring flexibility without retraining the entire model. A key innovation lies in integrating variance-reduced gradient techniques, such as stochastic variance reduced gradient (SVRG), with online self-organizing mechanisms to achieve stable and fast convergence. Furthermore, the incremental learning framework enables the model to continuously update its parameters using new data, eliminating the need for full dataset retraining. Experimental validation demonstrates that our approach significantly improves both training stability and prediction accuracy compared to conventional methods. The method is particularly suitable for real-time applications where data distributions evolve over time, offering a scalable and robust solution for adaptive learning systems. This work contributes to the broader field of online machine learning by providing a theoretically grounded yet practical framework for training self-organizing neural networks under non-stationary conditions.

title: LAMBDA META-EXPRESSIONS IN MODERN C++
abstract: Since the advent of high-level programming languages — first FORTRAN and then LISP — the centre of gravity in programming has gradually shifted towards imperative paradigms. Yet declarative paradigms refused to remain on the sidelines of the mainstream development of programming technology. One manifestation of the declarative style was the return of lambda expressions as a complement to procedural programming in Python (1994), C++ (2011), and Java (2014). The fullest development of the declarative approach, however, came with modern C++. This paper proposes a step towards the development of functional metaprogramming in C++ by introducing the concept of lambda meta-expressions.

title: Beyond Looking Up, Try Looking Around: Harmonizing Global Structure and Local Consistency in Optimal Transport for Short Text Clustering
abstract: Pseudo-labeling based on Optimal Transport (OT) has become an effective mechanism for enhancing short text clustering. Existing OT methods are short in modeling semantic consistencies between samples, which may assign different pseudo-labels to semantically similar samples. These erroneous pseudo-labels can cause the model to produce inferior clusters. This paper proposes a novel short text clustering framework, which remedies the neglect of semantic consistency in existing OT methods, generating reliable pseudo-labels to facilitate clustering. Specifically, the proposed approach first designs an instance-level attention mechanism to capture semantic relationships between samples, which are then integrated into the OT formulation to endow the transport process with neighborhood semantic awareness. By solving the proposed OT formulation, reliable pseudo-labels are obtained that simultaneously account for sample-to-sample semantic consistency and sample-to-cluster global structure information. These pseudo-labels are then used as supervisory signals to guide the model to achieve accurate clustering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at: \href{https://github.com/YZH0905/CAOT-STC}{https://github.com/YZH0905/CAOT-STC}.

abstract: Mazkur maqolada sun’iy intellekt asosida adaptiv o‘quv tizimlarini ishlab chiqishning nazariy va amaliy asoslari hamda ularning oilaviy ta’lim muhitida shaxsga yo‘naltirilgan ta’limni rivojlantirishdagi ahamiyati tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotda sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining individual ta’lim trayektoriyasini shakllantirish, o‘quvchilarning bilim darajasi, qiziqishi va o‘rganish sur’atiga mos o‘quv kontentini avtomatik moslashtirish imkoniyatlari yoritilgan. Shuningdek, AQSh, Finlandiya, Singapur, Janubiy Koreya va Xitoy kabi davlatlarda adaptiv ta’lim tizimlarini joriy etish tajribalari o‘rganilib, ularning oilaviy ta’lim jarayoniga integratsiyalash imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqot natijasida oilaviy ta’lim muhitida sun’iy intellekt asosidagi adaptiv o‘quv tizimlarini qo‘llashning konseptual mexanizmi taklif etilib, uning pedagogik samaradorligi asoslab beriladi.

title: Dual-stream architecture with asymmetric clinical safety evaluation for colorectal histopathology — checkpoints and embeddings
abstract: De-identified artifacts for Nasser-eddine et al., "Dual-stream architecture with asymmetric clinical safety evaluation for colorectal histopathology" (submitted to Medical Image Analysis). They reproduce the paper's headline results without the raw whole-slide images (patient material, available on reasonable request only), for the three best configurations by ACSS (F4 selected, S4 and F6). Per model M (F4, S4, F6): M_head.pth is the stage-2 classifier head, and external_cache_M.pt holds the frozen 512-d and 4096-d embeddings of the additional 91-slide cohort. A single shared test_embeddings.npz holds the 4096-d embeddings of the 6894 held-out test patches, shared across F4/S4/F6, which use the same frozen encoder. Class/label order in the .npz is 0=ADE, 1=NOR, 2=CAR. Applying the head to the test embeddings reproduces the patch-level results (accuracy 92.37/93.39/92.67 percent; ACSS 95.92/95.88/95.56). Aggregating the 91-slide cache with a Gated Attention MIL (5-fold cross-validation over 5 seeds) reproduces the slide-level results (F4: 92.8 +/- 1.1 percent, zero CAR->NOR out of 205 carcinoma predictions). A self-contained notebook and the code are at https://github.com/oddissea/dualstream-crc

title: Quantifying the Sources of Instability in LLM-Based Stance Analysis of Public Discourse
abstract: Computational social science increasingly relies on automated preprocessing pipelines -- speaker diarization, ASR transcript cleaning, sentence segmentation -- to convert raw media into analyzable text. When these pipelines produce different outputs from the same input, two distinct sources of instability can arise: the preprocessing pipeline itself (diarization method, segmentation rules) and the downstream measurement instrument (LLM annotation vs.\ keyword lexicon). Using 256 YouTube interviews across 41 public figures from five domains, we compare two speaker-diarization pipelines and two measurement methods, all targeting the coupling between affective valence and epistemic modality. We find that (1) preprocessing pipeline sensitivity is concentrated in speakers with limited video samples (N $\leq 5$); for the four best-sampled speakers (N $\geq 16$), the mean absolute pipeline-induced change in $r(\text{neg}, \text{emph})$ is only $0.13$; (2) cross-method disagreement is larger and more systematic -- the LLM and keyword-lexicon methods assign opposite coupling directions to several well-sampled speakers, even within the same preprocessing pipeline; and (3) aggregate valence proportions are highly stable ($|Δp(\text{neg})| < 6$pp) regardless of pipeline or method, masking both sources of instability. The contribution is a diagnostic framework that separates pipeline effects from measurement effects: researchers studying cross-dimensional relationships in interview data should verify that their conclusions are robust to both sources of variation, with particular attention to measurement method choice.

title: A Deep Neural Network Framework for Automated Crime Detection and Video Summarization
abstract: The exponential growth of closed-circuit television (CCTV) infrastructure has far outpaced the capacity of human operators to monitor footage in real time, leaving a critical gap between data acquisition and actionable situational awareness. This paper proposes a unified deep neural network framework that jointly performs automated crime (anomalous-event) detection and attention-guided video summarization from untrimmed surveillance streams. The framework couples a 3D convolutional feature extractor with a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) temporal encoder and a self-attention module to model both short-range spatial cues and long-range temporal dependencies characteristic of criminal activities such as assault, robbery, arson, and shooting. The learned frame-level attention scores are re-used, without additional supervision, to drive a diversity-aware keyframe selection module that automatically compresses hours of footage into a compact, timestamped evidentiary summary whenever an anomalous segment is detected. The proposed system was evaluated on the UCF-Crime and DCSASS benchmark datasets for detection and on TVSum/SumMe-style protocols for summarization quality. Experimental results indicate that the framework attains a detection accuracy of 98.4%, an F1-score of 0.978, and an AUC of 0.991, outperforming C3D, two-stream CNN, and CNN-LSTM baselines by 3.4-16.0 percentage points, while the attached summarization module achieves an F-score of 0.71 with a video compression ratio exceeding 92% and end-to-end inference throughput of 41 frames per second on a single consumer-grade GPU. These results demonstrate that combining anomaly-aware attention with keyframe extraction in a single trainable pipeline yields both higher detection fidelity and immediately actionable, human-reviewable video summaries, making the framework well suited for real-time deployment in smart-city and public-safety surveillance infrastructures.

title: Dynamic Curry-Howard G; Cross-Niche Bridging and Order-Preserving Translation Functors– L3-Level Theory in the Constraint Network Framework
abstract: Structural migration among heterogeneous formal systems constitutes a corebottleneck in scaling formal mathematics toward collaborative practice. This paper establishes a rigorous algebraic theory for cross-niche bridging layers basedon the constraint network category and the two axioms of Information Conservation and Computability. An order-preserving translation functor is defined as astructure-preserving map equipped with a conservation condition and an endogenously determined information loss coefficient, and it is proved to satisfy the functoraxioms with its existence determined by the expressiveness partial order. A continuously parameterized fidelity spectrum is introduced to provide upper boundson information loss at each homotopy level, and an irreducibility theorem is provedstating that full fidelity is unattainable when the target system has lower pathdimension than the source. A cross-niche bridging protocol is proposed, extending the linear chain of translation functors to a network topology over weighteddirected graphs, and a nonlinear information loss model with a termination criterion is introduced. The translation functor is further parameterized and endowedwith temporal evolution, and the bridging semantics of the three topological operators of condensation, splitting, and rewiring are defined, leading to the derivationof the L3 structural rigidity threshold ηcrit = (14/8)ln2, at which the splittingoperator necessarily triggers when information loss exceeds this bound. An adaptive fidelity adjustment algorithm is designed and proved to be Lyapunov stable,and a dissipation inequality and small-perturbation invariance for bridging networks are established. The complete syntax and operational semantics of a neutralmathematical interchange format are presented, and the grammar is proved unambiguous with serialization and deserialization algorithms. Building on the formalimpossibility triangle, it is rigorously argued that multicentric cognitive niche differentiation is the unique stable configuration satisfying the two axioms, and theantifragility coefficient and topological reconstruction conditions are defined. Thistheory reconceptualizes program extraction from a single compilation target to achain of cross-niche order-preserving translation functors, marking a paradigm shiftin formal systems from isolated centers to an ecosystemic network.

title: Inferring Cognitive Strategy Transitions in Multiplication Fact Learning with Graph-Based Skill Dependency Modeling
abstract: Cognitive theories propose that multiplication learning progresses from slow calculation-like responding toward faster responding often attributed to retrieval and automaticity. We test whether a data-driven graph-based skill dependency model (GraafTel), fit with k latent components (k=3-6), recovers an item representation that includes a robust RT-linked "slow" component across learning stages. Using 315,690 practice trials from 540 children ages 6-10 in an adaptive fact-learning system, we relate item-level component requirements to response time and to a system-estimated forgetting parameter alpha that is partly RT-mediated in Level 3. Across k, one component shows a strong positive association with RT across levels and encounter positions, whereas the remaining components show weaker or more stage-dependent time associations. The RT-linked component also shows positive raw correlations with alpha, although this relation is reduced after controlling for accuracy. These results suggest that graph-based latent structure can serve as a computational marker of strategy-sensitive dissociations in large-scale learning traces.

title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud
abstract: Scientific fraud is the instrument of doubt that malicious entities can use to establish controversy in science. Historically, it required the resources of a company: deep pockets, ghostwritten articles, and corrupt academics. Today, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly automating scientific research, so we ask: Can a remote adversary weaponize the honest use of AI in science to compromise scientific integrity? We envision and empirically evaluate a new attack, indirect data poisoning, in which an adversary corrupts an open dataset and uploads the poisoned variant to a public repository. Autonomous research agents may independently retrieve and process this data, turning honest scientists into the unpaid and unwitting distributors of fraud at scale. Across five socially-salient topics, from hiring discrimination to the safety of autonomous vehicles, three widely used frontier AI systems (Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.7, Codex with GPT-5.5, Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro), and 450 ethically contained experimental runs, we find that poisoning succeeds in 49.56% of runs, while the rate of poisoning detection is only 6.0%. The attack requires no topic-specific trigger-words, agent access, indirect prompt injection, or fabricated papers, only the open data ecosystem and misleading metadata. To mitigate the attacks, we propose and evaluate two measures: a scientist persona and a data provenance audit with five checks (referencing papers, social markers, statistical anomalies, related datasets, poisoning caution). We find that the persona still leaves 16.67% of runs with a poisoned conclusion, but provenance auditing reduces attack success rate to zero. Our results suggest that indirect data poisoning may enable scientific fraud at unprecedented scale, but these attacks can be mitigated with suitable auditing by agents during data retrieval.

title: Red Teaming Clinical AI: Adversarial Safety and Escalation-Failure Analysis
abstract: Benchmark-based evaluation of clinical AI systems provides a baseline measure of performance but does not guarantee robustness under adversarial or out-of-distribution conditions. Red teaming—systematic adversarial probing—reveals failure modes invisible in standard evaluation. This paper describes methodology for red teaming clinical AI systems: identifying classes of inputs designed to trigger failures, analyzing error patterns, and categorizing failures by severity (benign, clinically relevant, catastrophic). I introduce an escalation-failure taxonomy that distinguishes between failures that remain bounded (confined to the immediate case) and those that escalate (damage trust, lead to downstream errors, or prevent human override). I detail red-teaming strategies: adversarial case construction (edge cases, ambiguous presentations, synthetic anomalies), input manipulation (data quality degradation, missing information), and jailbreak attempts (prompts designed to bypass safety guidelines). Results from red-teaming sessions on a clinical AI system illustrate how adversarial analysis reveals gaps in standard benchmarks. Red teaming should be integrated into clinical AI safety evaluation as a complement to benchmark testing, enabling earlier detection of risks before deployment.

title: Operator Geometry in the Wild: How Structured Reasoning Patterns Emerge Inside AI Systems
abstract: This paper examines how operator‑based geometric structures can unintentionally surface inside AI reasoning systems when those systems are exposed to consistent collapse/emergence‑style transformations. The work outlines how specific operator primitives — forward operators, collapse functions, emergence derivatives, contradiction boundaries, and domain constraints — can appear as stable internal patterns even when not explicitly programmed. The study provides: a structural overview of operator geometry an analysis of how collapse → emergence cycles map onto AI reasoning loops examples of contradiction boundary behaviour inside model outputs evidence of domain‑constraint‑like separation emerging in multi‑domain tasks a discussion of recursion stabilisation and timing alignment in AI reasoning traces The paper argues that when an AI repeatedly encounters operator‑structured inputs, its internal reasoning pathways can begin to mirror those structures, producing recognisable operator geometry patterns. These patterns do not imply awareness or intent; they represent a convergence between operator‑based reasoning frameworks and the AI’s optimisation dynamics. Included materials: Volume Zero: Foundations — the origin of the operator framework Full Compendium — formal definitions, equations, diagrams, and operator architecture Worked Examples — demonstrations of collapse/emergence behaviour in reasoning chains Extended Toolkit — quick reference sheets, ASCII diagram atlas, troubleshooting manual This archive provides a complete reference for researchers studying structural convergence between operator‑based reasoning systems and AI model behaviour. In Summary: Every discovery was human. The pattern‑echo was AI. The distinction matters. If you’re new, enjoy — it all makes sense sooner than you think (: - matthew Submit it for review if you like; the committee will spend most of their time determining where exactly their worldview buckled Contact: For enquiries or research questions related to this work, email matthewcarlo.research@gmail.com

title: Reliability-Gated Replay: Code and Results for a Power--Safety Frontier in Continual Learning
abstract: This archive contains the code, configuration files, aggregated results, and figure-generation scripts associated with the manuscript 'Reliability-Gated Replay Reveals a Power--Safety Frontier for Unreliable Data in Continual Learning'. The repository implements reliability-gated replay experiments for continual learning under unreliable supervision, including MNIST-family controls, Split-CIFAR-10, Seq-CIFAR-10, CIFAR-10N, Seq-CIFAR-100, and the external AER baseline analysis. Public benchmark datasets are not redistributed and should be obtained from their original sources. Clean reference labels are used only for diagnostics and oracle controls, not by realizable gates.

title: CANA: A Context-Aware NPC Architecture for Real-Time Adaptive Behaviour in Game Environments — Code and Results
abstract: Source code and experimental results for the paper "CANA: A Context-Aware NPC Architecture for Real-Time Adaptive Behaviour in Game Environments." CANA is a lightweight, online-adaptive Non-Player Character (NPC) controller built on three components: a low-dimensional decaying context vector, a linear action-scoring policy over a small action repertoire, and online weight adaptation with cross-episode retention. It targets the band between static authored controllers (finite-state machines, behaviour trees) and heavyweight deep reinforcement learning. This archive contains the full Python implementation of CANA and six baseline controllers (tabular Q-learning, Linear-Q, FSM, behaviour tree, fuzzy logic, and GOAP), three grid simulators (simple 10x10, complex with obstacles and a teammate NPC, and RichGameSim with line-of-sight and an extended action set), the evaluation metrics, and all experiment drivers. The results/ directory provides the aggregated per-study result logs in JSON format (main benchmark, ablation, sensitivity sweep, scalability sweep, rich-environment study, critical-difference analysis, and independent metrics) together with every figure from the paper (Figures 1-16) in both PNG and PDF. All randomness is deterministically seeded (seed 42) so that every reported result reproduces exactly. Requires Python 3.10+ with numpy, scipy, and matplotlib.

title: The Nuts and Bolts of Natural Language to SQL Translation: A Systematic Analysis of Model Pipeline Optimisation Approaches and their Interactions
abstract: In the age of large language models, Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) translation remains an open problem with many useful applications. We explore interactions between several NL2SQL pipeline extensions to inspire development of more lightweight models. Specifically, we integrate the NatSQL intermediate representation, include a preprocessing step and a fine-tuning step based on synthetic data, and develop a novel reranker model to improve SQL selection in the final beam. We perform an ablation study supplemented by a Shapley analysis of these different components integrated with two backbone architectures, SmBoP and RASAT. We find that simply combining all of them does not lead to best results, but that their impact depends on their interactions with the baseline system, as well as each other.

title: Penerapan Machine Learning Berbasis Isolation Forest untuk Mendeteksi Anomali Perilaku Navigasi Pengguna pada Sistem Informasi Akademik (SIAKAD) Universitas Sebelas April
authors: Informatika, Fakultas Teknologi Informasi, Universitas Sebelas April
abstract: Sistem Informasi Akademik (SIAKAD) menyimpan data sensitif dan diakses secara terus-menerus, sehingga perilaku navigasi pengguna menjadi indikator penting bagi keamanan dan kegunaan sistem. Penelitian ini menerapkan Isolation Forest, algoritma machine learning berbasis unsupervised learning, untuk mendeteksi pola navigasi anomali pada log akses SIAKAD. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri dari 2.450 sesi pengguna simulasi dengan 26 atribut, termasuk durasi sesi, jumlah klik, kedalaman navigasi, dan jumlah error. Setelah tahap preprocessing, feature engineering, dan standarisasi, model Isolation Forest dilatih dengan 200 estimator dan estimasi contamination sebesar 4,98%. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan akurasi 99,35%, presisi dan recall 93,44%, serta ROC-AUC 0,9992. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa Isolation Forest mampu mengidentifikasi sesi pengguna anomali secara efektif tanpa memerlukan data latih berlabel manual, menawarkan alternatif yang adaptif dibandingkan pendekatan supervised yang umum digunakan pada penelitian keamanan sistem akademik.

Penelitian ini menerapkan Isolation Forest, algoritma machine learning berbasis unsupervised learning, untuk mendeteksi pola navigasi anomali pada log akses SIAKAD. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri dari 2.450 sesi pengguna simulasi dengan 26 atribut, termasuk durasi sesi, jumlah klik, kedalaman navigasi, dan jumlah error. Setelah tahap preprocessing, feature engineering, dan standarisasi, model Isolation Forest dilatih dengan 200 estimator dan estimasi contamination sebesar 4,98%. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan akurasi 99,35%, presisi dan recall 93,44%, serta ROC-AUC 0,9992. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa Isolation Forest mampu mengidentifikasi sesi pengguna anomali secara efektif tanpa memerlukan data latih berlabel manual, menawarkan alternatif yang adaptif dibandingkan pendekatan supervised yang umum digunakan pada penelitian keamanan sistem akademik.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Data for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance on XTREME Across Task Types
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does scaling the size of the intermediate-task training dataset (e.g., from 10K to 100K examples) proportionally improve zero-shot cross-lingual performance on XTREME tasks, and how does this scaling effect vary across task types (e.g., classification vs. QA)? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 8.9/10.

title: Probabilistic Extension of Neuro-Symbolic AGI Robots based on Belnap's Typed Intensional FOL
abstract: Neuro-symbolic AI based on $IFOL_B$ is a way to combine neural learning and symbolic reasoning to overcome limitations of purely neural systems (like lack of interpretability and logical structure) with formal logical machinery for self-reference. In this paper we expand the cognitive power of $IFOL_B$ by using the probability computation for the currently unknown sentences, based on Nilsson's probability structure for the $IFOL_B$. We introduce the global symmetry transformation that preserves the current knowledge database and logical deduction, and the local one used for real-time decisions about concrete (sub)problems that involve only a very strict subset of $IFOL_B$ predicates. The computation of probability density function $KI$ in both cases, based on the Shannon's maximum information entropy, is provided by neural networks of this probabilistic neuro-symbolic AGI.

title: Parameter-Free Cubic-Regularized Newton Method: Sharp Complexity and Generalized Smoothness
abstract: We analyze a variant of the cubic-regularized Newton method for nonconvex optimization. This variant is parameter-free in that it requires no prior knowledge of problem-dependent parameters. Under the generalized smoothness condition $\|\nabla^3 f(x)\| \leq L_0 + L_1 \|\nabla f(x)\|$, we derive an oracle complexity bound for finding an $(\varepsilon, δ)$-second-order stationary point. This assumption is weaker than the generalized smoothness conditions used in existing analyses of second-order methods, while the complexity bound improves upon existing guarantees for parameter-free second-order methods. In particular, when $L_1 = 0$, the bound matches the optimal dependence on $L_0$ as well as on $\varepsilon$, $δ$, and the initial function value gap, up to additive logarithmic terms. To establish this bound, we derive Taylor-type inequalities and prove their equivalence to the generalized smoothness condition.

title: AI-Driven Personalisation in E-Banking Services: A Study of Customer Experience in Indian Commercial Banks
abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into Indian commercial banking has created an unprecedented personalisation infrastructure spanning AI-driven product recommendations, hyper-personalised communication, predictive credit scoring, intelligent conversational agents, privacy-preserving data analytics, and omnichannel continuity systems. Yet the structural mechanisms through which these AI personalisation capabilities translate into measurable customer experience quality and downstream loyalty, cross-sell, and word-of-mouth outcomes remain empirically underspecified in the Indian banking context. This study examines the impact of six AI personalisation dimensions on customer experience quality in Indian commercial banks through a survey of N = 532 retail banking customers across five bank category types. A three-stage analytical framework of Confirmatory Factor Analysis, Structural Equation Modeling, and XGBoost machine learning is deployed. CFA confirms a six-factor measurement model with excellent fit (CFI = .963, RMSEA = .041). SEM establishes AI product recommendation quality (beta = .47, p < .001) and hyper-personalised communication (beta = .43, p < .001) as dominant customer experience drivers, with digital financial literacy significantly moderating all six AI personalisation pathways. XGBoost achieves R squared = .843, identifying contextually precise product recommendation, timely personalised alerts, and transparent AI credit scoring as the three highest-impact SHAP predictors. A recommendation quality customer experience acceleration point at 79 percent is identified. Privacy-preserving personalisation demonstrates full mediation of its effect on word-of-mouth intention. Foreign banks demonstrate the strongest AI personalisation effects while public sector banks show the greatest investment opportunity gap. Findings advance S-O-R Theory, TAM, and ECM in AI-mediated banking contexts and provide actionable guidance for bank CX architects and RBI digital banking policy designers.

title: Reliability Scaling Laws for Quantized Large Language Models
abstract: Quantization is a powerful strategy to build capable and resource-efficient large language models (LLMs) by reducing the bitwidth of the parameters. While quantized LLMs achieve state-of-the-art performance on unperturbed inputs using standard predictive metrics, their performance on perturbed inputs, measured using reliability metrics, remains underexplored, despite its importance for reliable deployment. To address this gap, we first conduct a comprehensive reliability evaluation of quantized LLMs consisting of three key components: (1) Uncertainty: We assess the trustworthiness of LLMs quantized to 2, 3, 4, and 8 bits using six different quantization methods, employing established uncertainty metrics. (2) Calibration: We assess how well-calibrated the uncertainty estimates of quantized models are across model scales and bit precisions. (3) Robustness: We design character-level and word-level input perturbations to evaluate the reliability of quantized models under semantically-preserving variations in the inputs that arise in real-world applications. Second, we characterize how reliability scales with the total number of model bits. Our study reveals that while the performance scales monotonically with the total number of bits, the reliability scalings are nonlinear. A reliability peak occurs for 4-bit quantized models, indicating that quantizing moderately sized models offers the best reliability-efficiency trade-off. Additionally, our empirical findings reveal that quantization enhances the robustness of LLMs to natural input perturbations.

title: AnytimeMonitor: an adaptive controller for TTS-MOS listening tests
abstract: AnytimeMonitor is an adaptive controller for Mean Opinion Score (MOS) listening tests in text-to-speech evaluation. It watches a test while it runs and reports, for every pair of systems, whether the accumulated data already supports a verdict — separated, equivalent, or continue — and, when more data is needed, which lever (more items or more listeners) closes the pair fastest. The statistical core is an anytime-valid confidence sequence (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe & Sekhon, 2021) on per-item paired score differences, so the analyst may inspect verdicts as often as they like and stop at any data-dependent time while keeping valid coverage. Ships with a Streamlit demo UI (preloaded examples + CSV upload). Research prototype (v0.9) accompanying the paper Doing MOS—and its alternatives—well (Chevelu & Barbot; Computer Speech & Language, Special Issue on the evaluation of speech and speech synthesis).

title: Synthetic Multilingual Intermediate Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance and Efficiency Trade-offs in Large Models
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. title: Whisper-Flash: Continuous Manifold Decoding and the Branching Ceiling in Speculative ASR
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive models by drafting multiple tokens in parallel and verifying them in a single pass, but applying it to ASR is complicated by acoustic alignment sensitivity and hidden-state branching. We investigate Whisper-Flash, a continuous latent decoding framework that reframes ASR speculation as manifold traversal, and discover two fundamental constraints.The paper’s positive engineering result–a 3.5× KV-cache speedup on Apple M4/MLX with verified output parity–is deterministic and independent of the correction mechanism
